During load balance
column2: LBF_SOME_PINNED will be set if any candidate task

column1: cannot be detached due to CPU affinity constraints. This can result in
setting env->sd->parent->sgc->group_imbalance
column2: which can lead to a group

column1: being classified as group_imbalanced (rather than any of the other
group_type) when balancing at a higher level.
In workloads involving a single task per CPU
set due to per-CPU kthreads being the only other runnable tasks on any
given rq. This results in changing the group classification during
load-balance at higher levels when in reality there is nothing that can be
done for this affinity constraint: per-CPU kthreads
don't get to move around (modulo hotplug shenanigans).
It's not as clear for userspace tasks - a task could be in an N-CPU cpuset
with N-1 offline CPUs
column2: making it an ""accidental"" per-CPU task rather than

column1: an intended one. KTHREAD_IS_PER_CPU gives us an indisputable signal which
we can leverage here to not set LBF_SOME_PINNED.
Note that the aforementioned classification to group_imbalance (when
nothing can be done) is especially problematic on big.LITTLE systems
have a topology the likes of:
DIE [          ]
L  L  B  B
arch_scale_cpu_capacity(L) < arch_scale_cpu_capacity(B)
Here
column2: setting LBF_SOME_PINNED due to a per-CPU kthread when balancing at MC

column1: level on CPUs [0-1] will subsequently prevent CPUs [2-3] from classifying
the [0-1] group as group_misfit_task when balancing at DIE level. Thus
CPUs [0-1] are running CPU-bound (misfit) tasks
can significantly delay the upgmigration of said misfit tasks. Systems
relying on ASYM_PACKING are likely to face similar issues.
